Ad Bellum Administrativum · Defensor Marginis

Why companies call us

You didn't call because things are fine.

Executives already know how to build a company and execute. We teach them how to protect it. No gaps in the armor.

  • Margin fades between the bid and the close, and nobody can say where it went.
  • You pay to recruit and train people who leave inside ninety days.
  • Six figures go into client entertainment with no award to show for it.
  • You rent equipment while your own sits idle in the yard.
  • Decisions route around the policy, and changes come through the side door.
  • The field and the boardroom tell two different stories.

The approach

Three phases. Commit to one at a time.

Every phase ends at a signed gate. Savings count only when your own finance lead verifies them against a locked baseline.

PHASE 1 · 48 HOURS

Emergency Evaluation

Headquarters, offices and project sites, drilled at once. You get the Gap Brief and keep it, whatever you decide next.

  • The gaps, each with a dollar figure
  • Thirty-day moves to stop the bleed
  • The baseline for your finance lead
  • Who decides, and who resists
  • A one-year plan
PHASE 2 · DAYS 3–30

Stabilization

Tourniquets on, baseline locked, Task Force running. One owner for every gap and a weekly control gate.

PHASE 3 · MONTH 2 ONWARD

The Command Year

Three-month minimum, no maximum. Quarterly gate reviews, verified savings, leaders trained, and the procedures handed to your people so the gains hold after we leave.

The Mayormont Method

Seven tracks, drilled at once.

A conventional assessment studies one area after another. We drill every track in parallel, inside the same 48 hours, and every track feeds one Gap Brief.

Money

Where the cash and the margin leak, sized in dollars and locked into a baseline Finance signs.

People

The revolving door: who leaves, under which leader, what it costs, and the key chairs with no successor.

Business Development

Assets

Safety

We walk the ground. Protect the margin, and protect the people who build it.

Governance

Who really decides, where the approvals go around the policy, and one front door for change.

Doctrine

The Fiduciary Shield

The crest in front, the Laws behind it. Every gate, every cut and every hire is held to both sides.

THE FIDUCIARY SHIELD RULEEvery move passes one test: does it protect the enterprise margin, and does it protect the safety of the men in the mud?

The Laws of Command

Built like an arch: the Keystone holds the seven Laws in place. Each Law ends with a test you can run in four seconds. When two Laws pull against each other, the Keystone decides. Source: Administrative Warfare Field Manual, Laws of Command.

KEY

The Keystone: Never Change the Facts

You can frame a story. You can choose what to lead with, when to say it and how. You never change what happened.

The test: Is it true? Could you say it to their face? What does discovery find? What does it leave out?

I

Law I: Math Dictates Command

You do not perform miracles; you execute physics. Strip the panic away, pull the earned value data, and let the time impact analysis fight the battle.

The test: What does this cost in dollars, days and risk, and what does doing nothing cost?

II

Law II: Paper Is Armor

In the field, respect is earned with sweat. In the boardroom, it is enforced with ink. Never accept a verbal directive to alter the scope.

The test: If this goes to dispute in a year, what will the file say?

III

Law III: Feel Everything. Let Nothing Vote.

The Ice Wall isn’t the absence of feeling. It’s the refusal to let feeling hold the pen.

The test: What would I decide if I weren’t feeling this?

IV

Law IV: Build the Cage with Velvet

Never point the contract at a client like a gun. Give them a choice where every door leads somewhere they can live with.

The test: Can they say yes and still win in front of their own boss?

V

Law V: Never Put Your Feet on the Desk

Success is the silent killer of careers. Keep a perpetual sense of urgency, audit the green spreadsheets, hunt the hidden risks.

The test: When did I last see this with my own eyes?

VI

Law VI: Every Storm Is Terrain

Delays, strikes, hurricanes and lost bids are the ground the next plan is built on.

The test: What does this delay let us do that we couldn’t do before?

VII

Law VII: Replace Yourself to Rise

What you know keeps you in the trailer. What you teach lets you leave it.

The test: If I disappeared for thirty days, what would break?

Leadership

Julio Montemayor

Founder

Julio Montemayor founded Mayormont Capital & Command on a simple conviction: how a man leads in business cannot be separated from who he is when nobody is watching. Guided by his faith, a deep sense of higher accountability, and an uncompromising moral code, Julio views leadership not as a pursuit of status, but as an act of stewardship—answering first to God, to his family, and to the people carrying the weight on the front lines.

His character and operational code were forged in combat with 3rd Battalion, 3rd Marines and sharpened through the Special Operations Training Group (SOTG). In 3/3, he learned the reality of frontline brotherhood—where clarity under fire is a moral obligation and leaders share the burden of the men beside them. Through SOTG, that grit was tempered by surgical standards, relentless preparation, and an intolerance for shortcuts when everything is on the line. Out of that crucible came the principles that anchor MC&C: Never change the facts. Feel everything; let nothing vote. As the author of The Gap: Frontline Reality vs. Boardroom Delusion Strategy and Administrative Warfare, Julio rejects corporate theater and convenient illusions—choosing instead to stand at the front, shouldering the fiduciary shield to protect enterprises and the families whose livelihoods depend on them.

Before he is a founder, author, or strategist, Julio is a husband to his wife, Joseline, and a father to their children, Luna and Julito. Rooted in San Antonio, Texas, his life is measured by what endures: faith, loyalty, and presence—whether teaching his kids to ride on the dirt, sitting at the piano with his daughter, or building a legacy meant to outlast him. Every standard he brings to Mayormont Capital & Command is lived first under his own roof.
